question: A charity's operations analyst asks Claude to produce a requirements list for a new volunteer scheduling process, giving it only the notes from the two coordinators who happened to be available that week. The list reads as thorough and is circulated as the agreed requirements. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) Claude will refuse to produce a requirements list from notes covering part of the service
B) The two coordinators will be named in the list, exposing internal comments to everyone
C) The list will present gaps in the source notes as settled requirements nobody stated
D) The list will be too long for the sponsor to read before the decision has to be made
correct_answers: C) The list will present gaps in the source notes as settled requirements nobody stated
explanations: Claude will work with whatever it is given; it does not withhold an answer because the input covers only part of the service.
Attribution is a housekeeping matter and easily corrected; it does not affect whether the requirements themselves are real.

Correct. Claude will fill an incomplete picture with plausible, well-written material. Circulated as "the agreed requirements", inferred content becomes indistinguishable from what stakeholders actually asked for.
Length is a presentation problem. A concise list built on the same partial input would carry exactly the same defect.
